en: I used to think
zh: 我以前一直以为

en: the whole purpose of life was pursuing happiness.
zh: 人生的全部意义就是追求幸福。

en: Everyone said the path to happiness was success,
zh: 所有人都说，通往幸福的路就是成功，

en: so I searched for that ideal job,
zh: 所以我去寻找那份理想的工作，

en: that perfect boyfriend, that beautiful apartment.
zh: 那个完美的男朋友，还有那套漂亮的公寓。

en: But instead of ever feeling fulfilled,
zh: 可我非但没有感到满足，

en: I felt anxious and adrift.
zh: 反而感到焦虑又迷茫。

en: And I wasn't alone; my friends -- they struggled with this, too.
zh: 而且不只是我一个人这样，我的朋友们也在经历同样的挣扎。

en: Eventually, I decided to go to graduate school for positive psychology
zh: 最后，我决定去读积极心理学的研究生，

en: to learn what truly makes people happy.
zh: 想弄明白到底是什么真正让人幸福。

en: But what I discovered there changed my life.
zh: 但我在那里发现的东西，改变了我的人生。

en: The data showed that chasing happiness can make people unhappy.
zh: 数据显示，追逐幸福反而会让人不幸福。

en: And what really struck me was this:
zh: 而真正触动我的是这一点：

en: the suicide rate has been rising around the world,
zh: 全球的自杀率一直在上升，

en: and it recently reached a 30-year high in America.
zh: 而且最近在美国达到了30年来的最高点。

en: Even though life is getting objectively better
zh: 尽管从客观上看，生活正在变得更好，

en: by nearly every conceivable standard,
zh: 几乎从所有可以想到的标准来看都是如此，

en: more people feel hopeless,
zh: 却有更多人感到绝望，

en: depressed and alone.
zh: 感到抑郁和孤独。

en: There's an emptiness gnawing away at people,
zh: 人们内心有一种空虚感在不断啃噬着他们，

en: and you don't have to be clinically depressed to feel it.
zh: 而你并不需要达到临床抑郁的程度，也能感受到它。

en: Sooner or later, I think we all wonder:
zh: 我想，迟早有一天，我们都会问自己：

en: Is this all there is?
zh: 人生就只有这些了吗？

en: And according to the research, what predicts this despair
zh: 而根据研究，真正预示这种绝望的，

en: is not a lack of happiness.
zh: 并不是缺少幸福。

en: It's a lack of something else,
zh: 而是缺少另一种东西，

en: a lack of having meaning in life.
zh: 那就是缺少人生的意义感。

en: But that raised some questions for me.
zh: 但这又让我产生了一些疑问。

en: Is there more to life than being happy?
zh: 人生是否不只是快乐这么简单？

en: And what's the difference between being happy
zh: 幸福

en: and having meaning in life?
zh: 和拥有生命意义之间，到底有什么区别？

en: Many psychologists define happiness as a state of comfort and ease,
zh: 许多心理学家把幸福定义为一种舒适、轻松的状态，

en: feeling good in the moment.
zh: 也就是当下感觉良好。

en: Meaning, though, is deeper.
zh: 但意义感要更深层。

en: The renowned psychologist Martin Seligman says
zh: 著名心理学家 Martin Seligman 说，

en: meaning comes from belonging to and serving something beyond yourself
zh: 意义来自归属于并服务于超越自身的事物，

en: and from developing the best within you.
zh: 也来自发展出自己内在最好的部分。

en: Our culture is obsessed with happiness,
zh: 我们的文化痴迷于幸福，

en: but I came to see that seeking meaning is the more fulfilling path.
zh: 但我逐渐意识到，追寻意义才是更让人充实的道路。

en: And the studies show that people who have meaning in life,
zh: 研究也表明，生活中有意义感的人，

en: they're more resilient,
zh: 他们更有韧性，

en: they do better in school and at work,
zh: 在学校和工作中的表现也更好，

en: and they even live longer.
zh: 甚至寿命也更长。

en: So this all made me wonder:
zh: 于是这一切让我开始思考：

en: How can we each live more meaningfully?
zh: 我们每个人怎样才能活得更有意义？

en: To find out, I spent five years interviewing hundreds of people
zh: 为了找到答案，我花了五年时间采访了数百人，

en: and reading through thousands of pages of psychology,
zh: 还阅读了数千页有关心理学、

en: neuroscience and philosophy.
zh: 神经科学和哲学的资料。

en: Bringing it all together,
zh: 把这些内容整合起来之后，

en: I found that there are what I call four pillars of a meaningful life.
zh: 我发现，有四个东西构成了我所说的有意义人生的四大支柱。

en: And we can each create lives of meaning
zh: 而我们每个人都可以创造有意义的人生，

en: by building some or all of these pillars in our lives.
zh: 方法就是在生活中建立其中一些，或全部这些支柱。

en: The first pillar is belonging.
zh: 第一个支柱是归属感。

en: Belonging comes from being in relationships
zh: 归属感来自人际关系，

en: where you're valued for who you are intrinsically
zh: 在这种关系中，你因为真实的自己而被珍视，

en: and where you value others as well.
zh: 同时你也同样珍视他人。

en: But some groups and relationships deliver a cheap form of belonging;
zh: 但有些群体和关系提供的，只是一种廉价的归属感；

en: you're valued for what you believe,
zh: 别人看重你，是因为你相信什么，

en: for who you hate,
zh: 因为你仇恨谁，

en: not for who you are.
zh: 而不是因为你是谁。

en: True belonging springs from love.
zh: 真正的归属感源自爱。

en: It lives in moments among individuals,
zh: 它存在于人与人之间的一个个瞬间，

en: and it's a choice -- you can choose to cultivate belonging with others.
zh: 而且它是一种选择——你可以选择与他人一起培养归属感。

en: Here's an example.
zh: 举个例子。

en: Each morning, my friend Jonathan buys a newspaper
zh: 每天早上，我的朋友 Jonathan 都会买一份报纸，

en: from the same street vendor in New York.
zh: 从纽约同一个街头报贩那里买。

en: They don't just conduct a transaction, though.
zh: 不过，他们并不只是完成一笔交易。

en: They take a moment to slow down, talk,
zh: 他们会花一点时间慢下来，聊几句，

en: and treat each other like humans.
zh: 把彼此当作真正的人来对待。

en: But one time, Jonathan didn't have the right change,
zh: 但有一次，Jonathan 没有合适的零钱，

en: and the vendor said,
zh: 那个报贩就说，

en: "Don't worry about it."
zh: 没关系，不用给了。

en: But Jonathan insisted on paying,
zh: 可 Jonathan 坚持要付钱，

en: so he went to the store and bought something he didn't need
zh: 于是他跑去商店买了点自己并不需要的东西，

en: to make change.
zh: 只为了把钱换开。

en: But when he gave the money to the vendor,
zh: 但当他把钱递给报贩时，

en: the vendor drew back.
zh: 报贩却往后退了一下。

en: He was hurt.
zh: 他受伤了。

en: He was trying to do something kind,
zh: 他本来是想做一件善意的事，

en: but Jonathan had rejected him.
zh: 但 Jonathan 拒绝了他的好意。

en: I think we all reject people in small ways like this without realizing it.
zh: 我想，我们都会在不经意间，用这样的小方式拒绝别人。

en: I do.
zh: 我也会。

en: I'll walk by someone I know and barely acknowledge them.
zh: 我会从认识的人身边走过，却几乎不打招呼。

en: I'll check my phone when someone's talking to me.
zh: 别人跟我说话时，我会看手机。

en: These acts devalue others.
zh: 这些行为会贬低他人。

en: They make them feel invisible and unworthy.
zh: 它们会让别人觉得自己被忽视、不重要。

en: But when you lead with love, you create a bond
zh: 但当你以爱为出发点时，你就会创造一种联结，

en: that lifts each of you up.
zh: 这种联结会让你们彼此都被托举起来。

en: For many people, belonging is the most essential source of meaning,
zh: 对很多人来说，归属感是意义最重要的来源，

en: those bonds to family and friends.
zh: 也就是与家人和朋友之间的那些联结。

en: For others, the key to meaning is the second pillar: purpose.
zh: 而对另一些人来说，意义的关键在于第二个支柱：目标感。

en: Now, finding your purpose is not the same thing
zh: 找到你的目标，

en: as finding that job that makes you happy.
zh: 并不等同于找到一份让你快乐的工作。

en: Purpose is less about what you want than about what you give.
zh: 目标感更多关乎你能给予什么，而不是你想要什么。

en: A hospital custodian told me her purpose is healing sick people.
zh: 一位医院清洁工告诉我，她的目标是治愈病人。

en: Many parents tell me,
zh: 很多父母告诉我，

en: "My purpose is raising my children."
zh: 我的目标就是养育我的孩子。

en: The key to purpose is using your strengths to serve others.
zh: 目标感的关键，是用你的优势去服务他人。

en: Of course, for many of us, that happens through work.
zh: 当然，对我们很多人来说，这是通过工作实现的。

en: That's how we contribute and feel needed.
zh: 这就是我们做出贡献，并感到被需要的方式。

en: But that also means that issues like disengagement at work,
zh: 但这也意味着，像工作投入感低、

en: unemployment,
zh: 失业、

en: low labor force participation --
zh: 劳动参与率低——

en: these aren't just economic problems, they're existential ones, too.
zh: 这些并不只是经济问题，它们也是存在层面的问题。

en: Without something worthwhile to do,
zh: 如果没有值得去做的事情，

en: people flounder.
zh: 人就会迷失。

en: Of course, you don't have to find purpose at work,
zh: 当然，你并不一定要在工作中找到目标，

en: but purpose gives you something to live for,
zh: 但目标感会给你一个活下去的理由，

en: some "why" that drives you forward.
zh: 一个推动你向前的为什么。

en: The third pillar of meaning is also about stepping beyond yourself,
zh: 意义的第三个支柱，同样关乎走出自我，

en: but in a completely different way:
zh: 但它是以一种完全不同的方式：

en: transcendence.
zh: 超越感。

en: Transcendent states are those rare moments
zh: 超越状态指的是那些罕见的时刻，

en: when you're lifted above the hustle and bustle of daily life,
zh: 你仿佛被提升到日常生活的喧嚣之上，

en: your sense of self fades away,
zh: 自我感渐渐消退，

en: and you feel connected to a higher reality.
zh: 你感到自己与某种更高层次的现实连接在一起。

en: For one person I talked to, transcendence came from seeing art.
zh: 对我采访过的一个人来说，超越感来自欣赏艺术。

en: For another person, it was at church.
zh: 对另一个人来说，它发生在教堂里。

en: For me, I'm a writer, and it happens through writing.
zh: 对我来说，我是一名作家，而这种体验发生在写作中。

en: Sometimes I get so in the zone that I lose all sense of time and place.
zh: 有时候我会完全进入状态，以至于失去了对时间和地点的感知。

en: These transcendent experiences can change you.
zh: 这些超越性的体验可以改变你。

en: One study had students look up at 200-feet-tall eucalyptus trees
zh: 有一项研究让学生仰望200英尺高的桉树，

en: for one minute.
zh: 看一分钟。

en: But afterwards they felt less self-centered,
zh: 但之后，他们会变得不那么以自我为中心，

en: and they even behaved more generously
zh: 而且当有机会帮助别人时，

en: when given the chance to help someone.
zh: 他们甚至表现得更加慷慨。

en: Belonging, purpose, transcendence.
zh: 归属感、目标感、超越感。

en: Now, the fourth pillar of meaning, I've found,
zh: 现在，我发现意义的第四个支柱，

en: tends to surprise people.
zh: 往往会让人感到意外。

en: The fourth pillar is storytelling,
zh: 第四个支柱是讲述故事，

en: the story you tell yourself about yourself.
zh: 也就是你讲给自己听的、关于你自己的故事。

en: Creating a narrative from the events of your life brings clarity.
zh: 把你生命中的经历组织成一个叙事，会带来清晰感。

en: It helps you understand how you became you.
zh: 它帮助你理解自己是如何成为今天的自己的。

en: But we don't always realize that we're the authors of our stories
zh: 但我们并不总是意识到，自己就是人生故事的作者，

en: and can change the way we're telling them.
zh: 也可以改变讲述这个故事的方式。

en: Your life isn't just a list of events.
zh: 你的人生并不只是一串事件清单。

en: You can edit, interpret and retell your story,
zh: 你可以编辑、解读，并重新讲述自己的故事，

en: even as you're constrained by the facts.
zh: 即使你仍然受事实本身的限制。

en: I met a young man named Emeka, who'd been paralyzed playing football.
zh: 我认识了一个叫 Emeka 的年轻人，他在踢橄榄球时瘫痪了。

en: After his injury, Emeka told himself,
zh: 受伤之后，Emeka 告诉自己，

en: "My life was great playing football,
zh: 我以前踢橄榄球的时候，人生那么美好，

en: but now look at me."
zh: 可现在看看我。

en: People who tell stories like this --
zh: 那些这样讲述自己人生故事的人——

en: "My life was good. Now it's bad." --
zh: 我的人生曾经很好。现在却变糟了。

en: tend to be more anxious and depressed.
zh: 往往会更加焦虑和抑郁。

en: And that was Emeka for a while.
zh: Emeka 有一段时间就是这样。

en: But with time, he started to weave a different story.
zh: 但随着时间推移，他开始编织一个不同的故事。

en: His new story was,
zh: 他的新故事是：

en: "Before my injury, my life was purposeless.
zh: 受伤之前，我的人生没有目标。

en: I partied a lot and was a pretty selfish guy.
zh: 我经常参加派对，而且是个挺自私的人。

en: But my injury made me realize I could be a better man."
zh: 但我的伤让我意识到，我可以成为一个更好的人。

en: That edit to his story changed Emeka's life.
zh: 这次对人生故事的改写，改变了 Emeka 的一生。

en: After telling the new story to himself,
zh: 在他开始把这个新的故事讲给自己听之后，

en: Emeka started mentoring kids,
zh: Emeka 开始辅导孩子们，

en: and he discovered what his purpose was:
zh: 他也发现了自己的人生目标：

en: serving others.
zh: 服务他人。

en: The psychologist Dan McAdams calls this a "redemptive story,"
zh: 心理学家 Dan McAdams 把这称为'救赎型故事'，

en: where the bad is redeemed by the good.
zh: 也就是坏事被好事所弥补。

en: People leading meaningful lives, he's found,
zh: 他发现，那些活得有意义的人，

en: tend to tell stories about their lives
zh: 往往会讲述自己的人生故事，

en: defined by redemption, growth and love.
zh: 而这些故事由救赎、成长和爱来定义。

en: But what makes people change their stories?
zh: 但是什么会让人们改变自己的故事呢？

en: Some people get help from a therapist,
zh: 有些人会从治疗师那里获得帮助，

en: but you can do it on your own, too,
zh: 但你也可以自己做到，

en: just by reflecting on your life thoughtfully,
zh: 只要认真地回顾自己的人生，

en: how your defining experiences shaped you,
zh: 思考那些定义你的经历是如何塑造你的，

en: what you lost, what you gained.
zh: 你失去了什么，又得到了什么。

en: That's what Emeka did.
zh: Emeka 就是这么做的。

en: You won't change your story overnight;
zh: 你不可能一夜之间改写自己的故事；

en: it could take years and be painful.
zh: 这可能需要很多年，也可能会很痛苦。

en: After all, we've all suffered, and we all struggle.
zh: 毕竟，我们都受过苦，也都在挣扎。

en: But embracing those painful memories can lead to new insights and wisdom,
zh: 但接纳那些痛苦的回忆，可能会带来新的洞见和智慧，

en: to finding that good that sustains you.
zh: 让你找到那份支撑你继续走下去的美好。

en: Belonging, purpose, transcendence, storytelling:
zh: 归属感、目标感、超越感和讲述故事：

en: those are the four pillars of meaning.
zh: 这就是意义的四大支柱。

en: When I was younger,
zh: 我年轻的时候，

en: I was lucky enough to be surrounded by all of the pillars.
zh: 很幸运，身边就围绕着所有这些支柱。

en: My parents ran a Sufi meetinghouse from our home in Montreal.
zh: 我的父母在我们蒙特利尔的家里经营着一个苏菲派聚会场所。

en: Sufism is a spiritual practice associated with the whirling dervishes
zh: 苏菲派是一种灵性修行，常让人联想到旋转苦行僧，

en: and the poet Rumi.
zh: 以及诗人 Rumi。

en: Twice a week, Sufis would come to our home
zh: 每周两次，苏菲派信徒会来到我们家，

en: to meditate, drink Persian tea, and share stories.
zh: 一起冥想，喝波斯茶，分享故事。

en: Their practice also involved serving all of creation
zh: 他们的修行还包括服务世间万物，

en: through small acts of love,
zh: 通过一个个微小的爱之举动，

en: which meant being kind even when people wronged you.
zh: 这意味着即使别人伤害了你，也要保持善意。

en: But it gave them a purpose: to rein in the ego.
zh: 但这也给了他们一个目标：约束自我。

en: Eventually, I left home for college
zh: 后来，我离家去上大学，

en: and without the daily grounding of Sufism in my life,
zh: 生活里不再有苏菲修行每日带来的安定感，

en: I felt unmoored.
zh: 我感到漂泊无依。

en: And I started searching for those things that make life worth living.
zh: 于是我开始寻找那些让人生值得活下去的东西。

en: That's what set me on this journey.
zh: 正是这件事，让我踏上了这段旅程。

en: Looking back, I now realize
zh: 现在回头看，我才意识到，

en: that the Sufi house had a real culture of meaning.
zh: 那座苏菲之家确实有一种关于意义的文化。

en: The pillars were part of the architecture,
zh: 这些支柱就是它的结构的一部分，

en: and the presence of the pillars helped us all live more deeply.
zh: 而这些支柱的存在，也帮助我们所有人活得更深刻。

en: Of course, the same principle applies
zh: 当然，同样的原则也适用于

en: in other strong communities as well --
zh: 其他强大的社群——

en: good ones and bad ones.
zh: 无论是好的，还是坏的。

en: Gangs, cults:
zh: 帮派、邪教：

en: these are cultures of meaning that use the pillars
zh: 这些也是意义的文化，它们利用这些支柱，

en: and give people something to live and die for.
zh: 给人们某种值得为之生、为之死的东西。

en: But that's exactly why we as a society
zh: 但这恰恰说明，作为一个社会，

en: must offer better alternatives.
zh: 我们必须提供更好的替代选择。

en: We need to build these pillars within our families and our institutions
zh: 我们需要在家庭和制度中建立这些支柱，

en: to help people become their best selves.
zh: 帮助人们成为最好的自己。

en: But living a meaningful life takes work.
zh: 但过有意义的人生需要努力。

en: It's an ongoing process.
zh: 这是一个持续不断的过程。

en: As each day goes by, we're constantly creating our lives,
zh: 每一天过去，我们都在不断创造自己的人生，

en: adding to our story.
zh: 不断为自己的故事增添内容。

en: And sometimes we can get off track.
zh: 有时候，我们也会偏离方向。

en: Whenever that happens to me,
zh: 每当这种情况发生在我身上，

en: I remember a powerful experience I had with my father.
zh: 我就会想起和父亲之间一次震撼人心的经历。

en: Several months after I graduated from college,
zh: 大学毕业几个月后，

en: my dad had a massive heart attack that should have killed him.
zh: 我父亲突发严重心脏病，本来足以夺走他的生命。

en: He survived, and when I asked him what was going through his mind
zh: 他活了下来。后来我问他，在面对死亡时，

en: as he faced death,
zh: 他脑子里在想什么，

en: he said all he could think about was needing to live
zh: 他说，他唯一想到的就是自己必须活下去，

en: so he could be there for my brother and me,
zh: 这样才能陪在我和弟弟身边，

en: and this gave him the will to fight for life.
zh: 正是这个念头给了他为生命而战的意志。

en: When he went under anesthesia for emergency surgery,
zh: 当他接受紧急手术、进入麻醉状态时，

en: instead of counting backwards from 10,
zh: 他没有从 10 开始倒数，

en: he repeated our names like a mantra.
zh: 而是像念诵咒语一样，一遍遍重复我们的名字。

en: He wanted our names to be the last words he spoke on earth
zh: 如果他真的死去，他希望我们的名字，

en: if he died.
zh: 能成为他在世上说出的最后几个字。

en: My dad is a carpenter and a Sufi.
zh: 我父亲是一名木匠，也是一名苏菲派信徒。

en: It's a humble life,
zh: 那是一种朴素的人生，

en: but a good life.
zh: 但也是一种美好的人生。

en: Lying there facing death, he had a reason to live:
zh: 躺在那里直面死亡时，他有一个活下去的理由：

en: love.
zh: 爱。

en: His sense of belonging within his family,
zh: 他在家庭中的归属感，

en: his purpose as a dad,
zh: 他作为父亲的目标，

en: his transcendent meditation, repeating our names --
zh: 他超越性的冥想，也就是重复我们的名字——

en: these, he says, are the reasons why he survived.
zh: 他说，这些就是他活下来的原因。

en: That's the story he tells himself.
zh: 这就是他讲给自己的故事。

en: That's the power of meaning.
zh: 这就是意义的力量。

en: Happiness comes and goes.
zh: 快乐来来去去。

en: But when life is really good
zh: 但当生活真的很美好时，

en: and when things are really bad,
zh: 也当一切真的很糟糕时，

en: having meaning gives you something to hold on to.
zh: 拥有意义，会让你有所依靠。

en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢大家。
